newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE COULD FULFILL EMU CRITERIA AT END-98 - SANTER.
newsitem.headline: GREECE COULD FULFILL EMU CRITERIA AT END-98 - SANTER.

text.p: Greece's economy has made headway and could satisfy the convergence criteria for EMU participation at the end of 1998, said the president of the European Commission Jacques Santer.

"There are positive achievements in economic indicators and the climate is favourable and very positive so that the criteria could be satisfied at end-1998," said Santer after meeting with Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis.
Greece is the only EU country that does not satisfy a single convergence criterion so far but CPI inflation has been falling steadily in the first months of 1997 to 5.9 percent year-on-year in April.
Bond yields in the secondary markets have also dropped to around 9.5 percent and the drachma has been broadly stable against the ecu sliding about 1.0 percent year-to-date.

Greece's general government budget deficit stood at 7.4 percent of GDP in 1996 and is projected to fall to 4.2 percent of GDP in 1997 but its public debt to GDP ratio was still the third highest in the EU around 111 percent at the end of 1996.
Santer is visiting Athens to participate in the celebrations of Europe Day.
The president of the EU commission said there would be a new financial aid package for Greece beyond the year 2000 but allocations among member states had yet to be determined.
The commission will hand over its recommendations about the EU's enlargement and general financing proposals to the council of ministers and the European parliament in mid-July, said Santer.
EU's economic and social convergence should continue and be funded, said Simitis. --Costas Paris, Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
